cron_setup_guide_intro: This system needs ONE server cron entry. It runs Laravel's scheduler every minute, which fires all the scheduled tasks below. Background jobs are handled separately by the queue worker, set up further down this page.
cron_setup_step_ssh: SSH into your server and open the crontab editor
cron_setup_step_add_line: Paste the crontab entry below on a new line, save and exit.
cron_setup_step_verify: Wait 1-2 minutes, then press Refresh above — Cron Status should turn Active.
cron_not_running_warning: The server cron is NOT running. Scheduled tasks will not execute until it is set up. You can run any of them manually below in the meantime.
scheduled_tasks_intro: These run automatically once the cron is set up. You can also run any of them manually right now. Processing queued jobs is the exception: the queue worker does that continuously, and the button here is only to drain whatever is waiting now.
cron_task_spin_wheel_schedule_desc: Activates a scheduled spin wheel campaign at its start time (switching off the one it replaces) and retires campaigns past their end time.
cron_task_spin_wheel_codes_desc: Deactivates coupons won on the spin wheel once their validity has passed. Nothing is deleted, so past orders keep their record.
cron_job_spin_wheel_reward_desc: Tells a customer what they won on the spin wheel (mail, SMS, push and the in-app bell). Dispatched by the spin itself; the prize is already granted, so a stopped worker only delays the message.

cron_task_queue_desc: Drains the background jobs waiting right now: emails, push notifications, referral & cashback credits, bulk imports. Normally the queue worker does this on its own.
queue_worker_intro: Background jobs (emails, push notifications, referral and cashback credits, bulk imports) are handled by a worker that stays running. Set it up once with Supervisor, or any process manager your host offers, and it starts with the server and is restarted automatically if it stops.
queue_worker_step_open: Open your server's process manager — in aaPanel: App Store → Supervisor Manager.
queue_worker_step_paste: Add a new daemon for this project using the command below, or paste the whole configuration block.
queue_worker_step_start: Start it, and confirm the Pending Jobs count above stops growing.
supervisor_config_note: Save this as its own file in your Supervisor configuration directory, then reload Supervisor. Raise numprocs only if jobs pile up: each worker is another PHP process and another set of database connections.
queue_restart_note: A running worker keeps the old code in memory. The System Updater and the plugin installer signal a restart for you; run this by hand after any manual deployment.
queue_worker_fallback_active: This installation drains the queue from the minute scheduler (QUEUE_SCHEDULER_FALLBACK=true). That is meant only for hosting that cannot run a daemon: jobs wait up to a minute and every minute costs a full application boot. On a VPS, set up the worker below and set the value back to false.
queue_worker_stalled_warning: Jobs have been waiting for more than two minutes, so nothing is processing the queue. Emails, notifications and bulk imports are stuck until a worker runs. Set one up below, or use Run Now on “Process Queued Jobs” to clear what is waiting.
cron_task_cart_notification_desc: Sends abandoned-cart reminder push notifications to customers.
background_jobs_intro: These jobs are queued automatically by app events and executed by the queue worker — they are not run directly.

cron_job_bulk_emails_desc: Promotional emails composed in Admin > Emails, sent to many customers in the background.

cron_job_product_bulk_desc: Processes product bulk upload/update files with live progress.
cron_job_cart_reminder_desc: Scheduled reminder cycle for abandoned carts.
